questions.q: What is the WAL's role, per this lesson, and what SQL Server mechanism does it serve the same purpose as?
options: It's PostgreSQL's log-first record of every data change, serving the same purpose as SQL Server's transaction log
It's a cache of frequently-read pages, similar to the SQL Server buffer pool
It's PostgreSQL's index storage format
It's a backup file format equivalent to a .bak file
questions.explain: Every change is written to the WAL before the data files are touched — the same log-first discipline SQL Server's transaction log uses.

questions.q: What does setting archive_mode = on plus archive_command actually do?
options: Hands off each completed WAL segment to a command before it's eligible for recycling
Compresses the data directory automatically
Enables row-level security
Starts a streaming replica automatically
questions.explain: Without archiving, PostgreSQL recycles old WAL segments; archive_command captures them first so they can be replayed later.

questions.q: What does restore_command do during PostgreSQL recovery?
options: Fetches archived WAL segments back so they can be replayed
Deletes WAL segments that are no longer needed
Restores a logical pg_dump backup
Configures streaming replication credentials
questions.explain: restore_command is the mirror image of archive_command — it retrieves previously archived segments during a recovery.

options: The timestamp up to which PostgreSQL replays WAL before stopping
How often WAL segments are archived
The maximum size of a single WAL segment
The interval between automatic base backups
questions.explain: recovery_target_time tells PostgreSQL to replay WAL only up to that moment and stop, enabling point-in-time recovery.

questions.q: To recover a database to a point after your last base backup, what two things must you have?
options: A base backup and the continuously archived WAL segments since that backup
Only the latest pg_dump file
A streaming replica already running
Only the WAL segments, with no base backup needed
questions.explain: The base backup provides the starting point; archived WAL segments let PostgreSQL replay forward to any later target time.
